assumptions: Each objective column is a number where higher (maximize) or lower (minimize) is better.
Measured values are taken as exact.
limits: The first front does not choose for the user: which weighting of the objectives is right is a scientific judgement.
Two candidates whose values differ by less than measurement error are still ordered by those values.
With many objectives most candidates are non-dominated.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which candidates in a table does no other candidate beat on every objective at once, how deep does each of the rest sit, and which candidate beats it?

description: Which candidates in a table are not beaten on every objective at once: Pareto (non-dominated) sorting of rows scored on several columns, each to maximize or minimize. Returns each candidate's front (1 = non-dominated), the candidate one front up that beats it, and its crowding distance within its front (how isolated it is, so a short list can be spread along the front). Rows can be filtered first (`em_max>=580, agg=m`), and rows with an empty objective are left out and counted, never ranked last. moocore 0.3.2's pareto_rank and is_nondominated, emoa 0.5-3's and pymoo 0.6.2's crowding distances, reproduced.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

crowding.description: how isolation along a front is measured: NSGA-II's normalized distance (each gap over the objective's range, averaged), or the raw sum of gaps in each objective's own units. Values: normalised (NSGA-II (normalized)), raw (raw gaps). Advanced.

filter.description: keep only rows passing every clause, separated by commas: a column, one of = != >= <= > <, and a value (`em_max>=580, agg=m`). Numbers compare as numbers; a blank cell passes no ordering clause.

keep_duplicates.description: keep every copy of candidates with identical values on the first front; off keeps the first copy and names it as what the others duplicate. Advanced.

label.description: the column naming each candidate. Left unset, the first column.

maximise.description: the columns where higher is better, separated by commas.

minimise.description: the columns where lower is better, separated by commas.

order.description: what orders candidates within a front: crowding distance (how isolated each is), or exclusive hypervolume contribution (how much of the objective space the front loses without it). Values: crowding (crowding distance), hypervolume (hypervolume contribution).

reference.description: the hypervolume's reference point, one `column=value` per objective (`brightness=0, maturation=500`), each worse than every candidate. Left unset, each objective's worst value pushed out by 10% of its range. Only applies when order is hypervolume. Advanced.

table.description: the candidates: a header row, then one row per candidate. Comma- or tab-separated, quoted cells allowed.

name: rank_tradeoffs

counts.description: rows in the table, filtered out, left out for an empty objective, ranked

front.description: the non-dominated candidates (front 1), most isolated first

fronts.description: how many candidates sit on each front

hypervolume.description: the objective space front 1 dominates up to the reference point (hypervolume order only)

order.description: what ordered candidates within a front: crowding or hypervolume

ranked.description: every candidate ranked: front, flag, crowding distance, the candidate that beats it, its objective values

reference.description: the reference point the hypervolume was measured from, and whether it was derived (hypervolume order only)
